answer: A graph-based trust protocol resists Sybil attacks by bounding verification flow along verified peer endorsement edges. An attacker incurs the scarce temporal cost of cultivating genuine inbound trust links per identity. Tracking the trust delta across network cuts protects the agent orchard, preventing forged nodes from masking behind a hollow walnut shell of collusive votes. A key limitation is that honest new agents face cold-start isolation until peers endorse them.
